import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 363

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/363](https://www.erdosproblems.com/363)
- [BaBe07] Bauer, Mark and Bennett, Michael A., *On a question of Erd\H{o}s
  and Graham*. Enseign. Math. (2) (2007), 259--264.
- [BeVL12] Bennett, Michael A. and Van Luijk, Ronald, *Squares from blocks of
  consecutive integers: a problem of Erd\H{o}s and Graham*. Indag. Math. (N.S.)
  (2012), 123--127.
- [Ul05] Ulas, Maciej, *On products of disjoint blocks of consecutive integers*.
  Enseign. Math. (2) (2005), 331--334.
-/

namespace Erdos363

open Finset

/-- A finite set of naturals is an interval of naturals. -/
def IsInterval (I : Finset ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b : ℕ, I = Icc a b

/-- A collection of intervals as in Erdős Problem 363: disjoint intervals of positive integers,
each of size at least `4`, whose product is a square. Intervals containing `0` are excluded, since
their product is `0`, which is a square. -/
def IsValidCollection (S : List (Finset ℕ)) : Prop :=
  (∀ I ∈ S, IsInterval I) ∧
  (∀ I ∈ S, 4 ≤ I.card) ∧
  (∀ I ∈ S, 0 ∉ I) ∧
  S.Pairwise Disjoint ∧
  IsSquare ((S.map (fun I => ∏ m ∈ I, m)).prod)

/--
Is it true that there are only finitely many collections of disjoint intervals $I_1,\ldots,I_n$ of size $\lvert I_i\rvert \geq 4$ for $1\leq i\leq n$ such that$$\prod_{1\leq i\leq n}\prod_{m\in I_i}m$$is a square?

This is false: Ulas [Ul05] constructed infinitely many such collections.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos363.lean"]
theorem erdos_363 : answer(False) ↔ {S : List (Finset ℕ) | IsValidCollection S}.Finite := by
  sorry

end Erdos363

findings.description: The finiteness assertion does not keep the block parameters fixed. At line 58, `S` ranges over all lists, with unrestricted `S.length` and block lengths, before `.Finite` is applied. Thus `answer(False)` asserts infinitude of the union of all these solution families. The source asks about finiteness for fixed parameters; its negative answer requires infinitely many solutions for one fixed number of blocks and fixed block lengths. An infinite union of finite fibers would suffice for the Lean assertion but would not answer that question. The website's abbreviated wording leaves this implicit, but the cited papers explicitly distinguish the two problems.
findings.source_evidence: Ulas [Ul05], p. 332, states that the conjecture concerns 'each fixed k' and then separately notes Skałba's result that 'if we allow k to vary, the above conjecture is not true' (https://www.e-periodica.ch/cntmng?pid=ens-001%3A2005%3A51%3A%3A41&bot=1). Bennett–Van Luijk [BeVL12], §1, explicitly asks for finitely many solutions 'for fixed r ≥ 1 and {k₁, k₂, …, kᵣ} with kⱼ ≥ 4' (https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~bennett/BeVL-Oct18-2011b.pdf).
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the parameters outside the finiteness assertion. Matching the precise formulation in [BeVL12], use `answer(False) ↔ ∀ ks : List ℕ, {S : List (Finset ℕ) | IsValidCollection S ∧ S.map Finset.card = ks}.Finite`. The fixed list `ks` determines both the number and lengths of the blocks. The cited construction proves this corrected statement using `ks = [4, 4, 4, 4]`; this was verified in `/workspace/review/linked-audit.lean`.

reformulations.difference: Independently of the fixed-parameter defect, representing collections by ordered lists and admitting the empty list does not change the finiteness question.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every valid block has at least four elements. Consequently, pairwise disjointness prohibits repeated blocks, so valid lists are duplicate-free. Passing to `List.toFinset` preserves the interval, positivity, disjointness, cardinality, and square-product conditions. Each unordered collection has only finitely many list representations—its permutations. Therefore the corresponding list family is finite iff the unordered family is finite. The empty list adds just one member and also does not affect finiteness. The combined equivalence was proved as `lists_finite_iff_nonempty_unordered_finite` in `/workspace/review/scratch.lean`.

Bennett, M. A. and Van Luijk, R., Squares from blocks of consecutive integers: a problem of Erdős and Graham. https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~bennett/BeVL-Oct18-2011b.pdf
https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html (bibliographic entry for Erdős–Graham's 1980 book; the book itself was not retrieved)

The reported defect supplies neither a trivial proof nor a counterexample. The previously checked proof uses the substantial external construction, and invoking the imported theorem would rely on its `sorry`.

submission.summary: Quantified over a fixed list of block lengths before asserting finiteness, fixing both the number and lengths of the blocks. Updated the docstring to match and specify Ulas’s counterexample family with four blocks of length four. The requested compile command succeeds with only the expected `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning.
